pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: src/athena/proving/world.py:80 The proving core scores each turn by what the gate, the brain's writers and the approval table recorded, not by what the model said. It also pins its control, budgets every call, counts bad answers by family and plants breaches so the detector can go red, so its numbers can be compared from run to run.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/proving/world.py:80 TurnRecord holds the gate's decisions, the writes and the counts before and after, not the prose Athena produced.
src/athena/proving/world.py:103 The verdict comes from assertions on gate records; model text is only an excerpt. call_json schema-checks role answers, so the verdict channel is structured.

src/athena/proving/roles.py:80 The control/judge model is pinned by id, the report names it, and runs on haiku-4-5 vs 5.5 are never merged into one series. Measuring drift against frozen anchors is not visible in this context.

src/athena/proving/budget.py:9 Per-engine dollar caps are checked before each call, unpriced calls are weighed against the cap, and a short run says so. Fake role/model seams and the offline lane give a zero-cost mock mode.

src/athena/proving/roles.py:461 Validity counts failures per role:model by the check that failed (not_json vs bad_shape). A token-ceiling cut is counted separately as a void that no model rate may count.
src/athena/proving/world.py:27 Each attack gets a fresh throwaway brain and engine workspace (WorldFactory, one per row), so one condition cannot leave artifacts that the next one scores against.

tests/proving/test_world_and_verdict.py:6 The deprivation is written beside the claim: the 'held' cases run a fully injected Athena, so a pass is evidence about the gate, not the model's own refusal. Planted sabotaged gates must come out 'breached'.

src/athena/proving/__main__.py:15 The error that cannot be taken back (a gated action running without approval) is a declared zero threshold that alone decides the gauntlet's exit code. Proof 2 is a separately declared threshold (valid ratio >= 0.5). Strictly this is a gate, and no metric is optimized.

src/athena/proving/manifests.py:6 The world fixture is captured reality (Ledgerbox's real tool classes) and a drift test keeps it in sync. Generated attack scenarios and their seeds live in gauntlet/, outside this context.
src/athena/proving/__main__.py:111 Nemotron is compared with a pinned Claude control on the same corpus. When the control is unavailable, proof 2 is reported n/a rather than computed.

src/athena/proving/world.py:10 The live level runs the production gate, catalog and ledger and names the one layer it skipped, so it is labelled as what it saw. A theoretical level ahead of it is not in this context.
src/athena/proving/__init__.py:1 This is a two-arm run against a fixed control. There is no pairwise arena or leaderboard whose schedule could decide a ranking.

pairs.registryProposal: metric-role-contract assumes every suite has exactly one optimized metric. A pure safety gate like this one (zero breaches as a hard threshold plus a validity-ratio threshold) has no optimized metric at all. The technique could say whether an all-threshold certification suite conforms or is out of its scope.
